items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had had so much enjoyment drinking and jamming with him.

ctx.x: He informed me that some of the orchestra were staying at the same place we were which was a very big rooming-house called the White House, because it was painted white. There was a room with a piano and one could buy bootleg whisky there. So we went to the White House after the dance which finished at 2 a.m. and started a jam session. The tenor sax in the Blue Devils band was a light-skinned, red-headed fellow and he told me his name was Lester Young.

Booker Pitman, Alfred Pratt and Leroy Hardy used to practice in between most of the shows and so did I. When the jam session was announced we were the only ones in the Cooper orchestra who sat in. I didn't remember any of the other musicians in the Blue Devils except George Hutchinson (whom I already knew) and Lester Young. I remember Lester because I had had so much enjoyment
drinking and jamming with him. I suppose his playing had made an impression on me without my really realizing it at the time.
